verdict.rationale: Gazebo documents first-party ROS integration: ros_gz is installed matched to your ROS version, and Gazebo ships as ROS 2 vendor packages from Jazzy onward. That points to robot code written against ROS being able to drive the simulator. However, the evidence never states that the same code runs unchanged on real hardware. It also never describes how topics or interfaces are bridged so that simulation and the real robot can be swapped. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the sim-to-real code portability workflow, a description of the ros_gz bridge mapping simulated sensors and actuators to standard ROS interfaces, hardware-abstraction or controller-interface parity details, and independent or hands-on corroboration of running identical code in simulation and on the real robot.
